description: Preparing agricultural land by ploughing, tilling, and leveling the soil before sowing crops to create suitable conditions for healthy plant growth.
Loosening and turning the soil using a plough or tractor to improve aeration and prepare the land for cultivation.
Making the field surface even after ploughing to create an even surface for irrigation and crop growth.
Preparing a fine, loose, and fertile soil bed by breaking clods and removing debris before sowing seeds.
Removing weeds and unwanted vegetation from agricultural land before cultivation to prepare the field for farming.
Selecting healthy, disease-free, and high-quality seeds suitable for cultivation to achieve better germination and crop yield.
Treating seeds before sowing to protect them from diseases and pests and to improve germination and early plant growth.
Placing seeds into the prepared soil at the correct depth and spacing for healthy crop establishment.
Moving young plants from a nursery or seedbed to the main field while maintaining proper spacing for healthy crop growth.
Growing and caring for young plants in a nursery until they are ready for transplanting into the main field.
Supplying water to crops at the right time and in the required quantity using methods such as canals, sprinklers, or drip irrigation to support healthy plant growth.
Providing essential nutrients to crops by applying fertilizers or organic compost to improve plant growth and increase yield.
Applying natural manure or compost to enrich soil fertility and improve crop productivity.
Removing unwanted weeds from agricultural fields to reduce competition for water, nutrients, and sunlight.
Covering the soil around crops with organic or inorganic materials to conserve moisture, suppress weeds, and regulate soil temperature.
Protecting crops from harmful insects and pests by using pesticides or other suitable control methods.
Preventing and controlling plant diseases through proper crop care and timely protective measures.
Regularly observing crop health, growth, weather conditions, and field conditions to identify problems and ensure proper crop management.
Removing unnecessary branches or plant parts to improve plant health, growth, and productivity.
Growing different crops on the same land in successive seasons to improve soil fertility and reduce pests and diseases.
Collecting mature crops from the field at the right stage to obtain maximum yield and quality.
Separating grains from harvested crops using manual methods or threshing machines.
Reducing the moisture content of harvested crops by drying them under sunlight or using drying methods to improve storage life.
Storing harvested crops under suitable conditions to protect them from moisture, pests, and spoilage.
Moving harvested crops safely from the field to storage facilities or markets for distribution.
Packing harvested agricultural produce properly to protect it during storage and transportation.
Managing dairy animals such as cows and buffaloes to produce milk and other dairy products through proper feeding, breeding, and healthcare.
Raising chickens for the production of eggs and meat while ensuring proper nutrition, shelter, and disease control.
Breeding and managing goats for the production of milk, meat, and other agricultural benefits through proper care and feeding.
Managing cattle by providing proper feeding, shelter, healthcare, and breeding to improve livestock productivity.
